gyreBoundaryCurrents.title: One basin, two unequal margins
gyreBoundaryCurrents.subtitle: Wind closes the surface water into a loop; rotation decides which side of the basin gets the fast lane.
gyreBoundaryCurrents.aria: Basin-scale ocean gyre with the western margin running {west} times the speed of the interior

slider.gradient: How much rotation's grip changes with latitude

verdict.symmetric: A fair racetrack: the loop spends the same time on either margin.
verdict.intensified: The loop lingers on the eastern side and sprints down the western one.

hint.symmetric: With rotation gripping equally at every latitude, the gyre is symmetric — both long margins the same width, water crawling around each. No ocean on a rotating world looks like this.
hint.intensified: Because rotation's grip strengthens with latitude, the return flow is crowded against the western margin: a narrow, deep, fast current there and a broad, slow drift on the far side. Earth's Gulf Stream and Kuroshio are the western kind; the California and Humboldt currents the eastern.

codaRhythmComparator.title: The message is the timing
codaRhythmComparator.subtitle: Every click is the same sound. What separates one vocal clan from another is only where the clicks fall in time.
codaRhythmComparator.aria: Click-timing tracks comparing vocal repertoires, showing {voice}
codaRhythmComparator.unresolved: Canon translates it; canon never diagrams it

limit.regular: Held for decades; not written in the genes
limit.plusOneOneThree: Shares maternal lineages with the others, never their company
limit.short: Kept distinct across decades of recording
limit.tulkun: No grammar has been shown, only meaning asserted

hint.clan: Sperm-whale clans are named for these rhythms. The clicks themselves are interchangeable broadband pulses; the pattern of silences is the whole signal.
hint.sympatric: These clans use the same water at the same time and share maternal lineages, yet units only ever associate with others that keep their rhythm. A difference no wider than a pause is doing the work of a social border.
hint.tulkun: Canon gives tulkun low rumbles that carry across an ocean basin, and subtitles them as sentences. It never exposes a structure. The band stays unresolved on purpose — the film asserts the meaning without showing the code.

signatureNote.regular: Five to eight clicks at a steady interval
signatureNote.plusOneOneThree: Two isolated clicks, then a rapid triplet
signatureNote.short: Three or four clicks packed close together

readout.gapNote: The whole difference between clans lives in numbers this small

elderMemoryLedger.title: What a pod loses with its oldest members
elderMemoryLedger.subtitle: Some knowledge only exists in an animal that lived through a bad year. Take those animals away and the pod forgets far faster than it shrinks.
elderMemoryLedger.aria: Pod age structure; the surviving pod's chance of still holding a lean-year memory is {pct} per cent
elderMemoryLedger.ageAxis: Age of each pod member, in years
elderMemoryLedger.glowNote: The brighter the body, the more lean years it has crossed

controls.recurrence: How rare a lean year is

verdict.held: Somebody alive has crossed a year like that before.
verdict.lost: Probably nobody left has crossed a year like that.

hint.intact: Every member alive. The oldest animals have crossed the most lean years, so the pod's rarest knowledge sits with them — and is safe only while they are.
hint.asymmetric: Compare the top two numbers. The head count barely moved; the pod's lived experience fell several times further, because experience piles up at the old end. A hunt that takes the oldest animals is not taking an average sample.
hint.buffered: At this recurrence, lean years come often enough that younger adults have crossed one too, so the pod's knowledge survives losing its elders. Make the lean year rarer and that buffer disappears.

reefRugosityProfile.title: The folds are the habitat
reefRugosityProfile.subtitle: Lay a chain over the reef and divide its length by the distance it spans. That one number predicts how much life the ground can hold.
reefRugosityProfile.aria: Cross-section of a reef surface with a measured roughness index of {index}

readout.rugosityNote: 1.0 is a flat floor; healthy reefs reach 2.5 and above
readout.refugesNote: Every valley deep enough to shelter something
readout.swellNote: What reaches the lagoon behind the reef

hint.complex: A branching framework folds far more surface into the same footprint. Each fold is a refuge from a predator, a nursery for something small, a place for something else to settle — and it dissipates the swell before it reaches the village.
hint.reduced: The finest structure goes first. Twigs, then branches, then boulders: as the framework is ground down, the smallest shelters disappear before the reef looks visibly damaged, and more swell starts getting through.
hint.flattened: At an index near 1.0 the reef is still there as rock and gone as habitat. The crevices have filled, the animals that lived in them have nowhere to be, and the swell the terraces used to break rolls straight through.
